target_customer: Schools, universities and other building owners who need indoor gunshot detection tied to fire alarm and emergency systems
problem: Active shooter incidents inside buildings are detected late, delaying lockdown and first responder alerts.
business_model: Hardware detectors sold with installation and a subscription or reporting network service
product_category: Indoor gunshot detection and emergency response hardware

founders.name: James Popper
founders.background_notes: YC page founder section is empty. Search summaries of Business Insider and CB Insights name Popper as CEO and Peter Street as co-founder; I could not open those pages, so roles are unverified.

founders.name: Peter Street
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in a Business Insider summary seen via search; unverified.

technical_complexity.rationale: Combining percussion, audio and infrared sensing to cut false alarms needed custom hardware and signal processing.

defensibility.rationale: The company advertises patented gunshot detection and integration with fire alarm and access control systems.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not established from sources found; no acquisition or copying reported.

market_need_then: Business Insider (2016) reported the system being installed on college campuses, indicating demand from schools after repeated shootings.

branding.domain_note: Uses amberbox.com exact match; no history found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Safety focused and technical: false alarms near zero

branding.community_and_virality: Business Insider ran a feature on the product; no merch or fan community.

brand_strength.rationale: Name suggests an amber alert and a box device, but no sourced evidence of brand driven growth.

outcome_analysis: AmberBox is listed as active and promotes a tri factor detector sold into schools and facilities. It raised an estimated 2 million dollars per aggregators and no shutdown or acquisition was found. With limited public reporting after 2016 there is not enough evidence to judge how well it scaled against rivals such as Shooter Detection Systems.
